newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea says grain supplies half what needed.
newsitem.headline: North Korea says grain supplies half what needed.

text.p: North Korea said on Monday that flood damage had left it with about only half of the food grain it needs to feed its people.

In an unusually detailed and frank description of the country's plight, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said North Korea "has in recent years been repeatedly hit by unprecedented natural disasters, which greatly damaged agriculture and other sectors of the national economy and caused temporary food problems".
"The nation's annual demand for grain is about 7.84 million tons, of which 4.82 million tons is needed as food," KCNA quoted a spokesman for the country's Flood Damage Measures Committee as saying.
"Last year's flood damage made the grain output drop to 2,502,000 tons in unhulled state, the amount being far less than expected," KCNA said in a report monitored in Tokyo.

The Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said last week that food rations across North Korea had dropped to a level four times lower than was normally considered essential to maintain a healthy population.
